    //==
    // # Operators over a strut list
    //
    // Grading, trimming and warping all consume the welded strut list rather
    // than re-tiling, so they compose in any order and none of them is a second
    // tiling path. Read left to right: `lattice.Struts.Trimmed(solid)` is the
    // trimmed lattice, and `.StrutRadii(field)` grades whatever it is handed.

    // One radius per strut, all the same. The uniform case in the shape the
    // graded operators produce, so the two feed the same consumers.
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: Number): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s => radius);
```

## Line 500

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/lattices.library.plato, line 500](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/lattices.library.plato#L500).

    // One radius per strut, read from a scalar field at the strut's midpoint.
    // The field's value IS the radius, in world units; nothing rescales it.
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: IScalarField3D): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s => radius.Eval(s.Centroid));
```

## Line 505

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/lattices.library.plato, line 505](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/lattices.library.plato#L505).

```plato

    // One radius per strut, from a grading field whose value is a fraction: the
    // field is sampled at the strut midpoint, clamped to [0, 1], and used to
    // interpolate between the ends of `range`. The usual spelling for "thicker
    // where this field is high".
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, grading: IScalarField3D, range: NumberInterval): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s =>
            range.Start.Lerp(range.End, grading.Eval(s.Centroid).Max(0.0).Min(1.0)));
```
